- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent prices are trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in price (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is positive — apply a “cool-down” correction by 5-10% in next 3-5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — apply a downward bias correction starting from the shift point.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2-5% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to dampen overfitting.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often underperforms — increase forecast by 2-5% to account for latent volatility.
